chapter: Kansas City rooms and Piney Brown
title: The Yellow Front, a jam-session room at 18th and Forest
summary: Lovett played there about two years from eight to five with Robert Thomas on trumpet and Emil Williams on piano.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Now to go into the interview here at the Afterhours. We were talking about some of the old rooms in Kansas City that Baby played and that Crook played and we came along with one; I thought I'd heard about most of them with my band, traveling with my band, they talked about the rooms and the people so much, but here is one called the Yellow Front, which is around 18th and Forest, where the bands used to play and it was a great place for jam sessions. Could you tell us more about the Yellow Front, Baby? Well, what happened down at the Yellow Front? I understand they used to jam down there?

Oh yes, we would start playing around eight o'clock and we'd play until five o'clock in the morning and everybody was jumping, having a good time and that was one of the greatest times of my life in the music business, playing at the Yellow Front, and they had a lady bouncer by the name of --
You talked about that in another room, the Babylon Club. Not down there, she wasn't down there. You talked about that last week.
How long did you play there, Baby? How

Well I think about a couple of years. It wasn't very long, about two years.
The cats used to come in and jam there?
Oh yeah, yeah we had a ball.
Remember who was on the band with you there? Was "Booster" there, your pal from Louisiana?
Yes, Booster was on trumpet.
What was Booster's full name?
Robert Thomas.
Robert Thomas?
That's right.
He came up from Louisiana with you --
Right.
-- and he played with you all the time -- well for a long time before he left town?
That is right, uh-huh, and Emile Williams played piano.
Oh, I've heard of him.
Oh yeah, he was a wonderful piano player. Everybody was crazy about him and we had a bouncer there called Eva Tangway.
